title: Hobbies
goal: Ask about someone's interests, explain what you do for fun, and talk about starting or continuing a hobby.

runs.text: A hobby conversation can begin with a broad question:
What do you do for fun?
At work,
What do you do outside of work?
makes the topic clear.
Do you have any hobbies?
is another option. An answer can be a short activity, not a complete life story.
Useful activity combinations include
play tennis
play the guitar
go hiking
do photography
make pottery
, and
play video games
. Choose activities you actually want to discuss. Chapter 26 offers more vocabulary; you do not need its whole list here.

turns.speaker: A

runs.text: What do you do for fun?

turns.en: What do you do for fun?

turns.speaker: B

runs.text: Mostly photography. I like taking pictures of buildings. How about you?

turns.en: Mostly photography. I like taking pictures of buildings. How about you?

turns.speaker: A

runs.text: I play guitar, but I'm still learning.

turns.en: I play guitar, but I'm still learning.

turns.speaker: B

runs.text: Oh, nice. What kind of music do you play?

turns.en: Oh, nice. What kind of music do you play?

turns.speaker: A

runs.text: Mostly rock. A few country songs, too.

turns.en: Mostly rock. A few country songs, too.

runs.text: Mostly
identifies your main activity without suggesting it is the only one.
I'm still learning
lets you talk about an interest without presenting yourself as an expert. A follow-up question responds to what the other person said; it need not introduce an entirely new topic.
I've started running
focuses on a recent start.
I've taken up painting
also presents painting as a new activity.
I'm trying out a pottery class
leaves open whether you will continue.
I've started taking dance classes.
Really? How's it going?

turns.speaker: A

runs.text: It's fun, but the steps are hard to remember.

turns.en: It's fun, but the steps are hard to remember.

runs.text: Would you recommend the class?

turns.speaker: A

runs.text: Yeah, if you don't mind being a beginner!

turns.en: Yeah, if you don't mind being a beginner!

runs.text: You can give a mixed opinion:
I like it, but it's challenging.
To show interest, try
That sounds fun
How did you get into it?
, or
What do you like about it?
You do not have to pretend you share the interest:
I've never tried that. What's it like?
keeps the conversation going honestly.
How long have you been playing?
asks about an activity continuing over time. Useful replies are
For about a year
Since last summer
, and
I only started last month
For
introduces a length of time;
since
introduces a starting point. Learn the question and your chosen answer as a usable pair.

turns.speaker: A

runs.text: How long have you been playing tennis?

turns.en: How long have you been playing tennis?

turns.speaker: B

runs.text: For about two years. I usually play on weekends.

turns.en: For about two years. I usually play on weekends.

runs.text: Want to play sometime?
Maybe. I'm pretty rusty, though.
Rusty
here means out of practice. The tentative
Maybe
does not confirm a plan; a definite arrangement needs a time and agreement, as in Chapter 12.
Practice alone by reading the question, covering the answer, and replying aloud. Then speak both parts. With someone else, switch roles.
Use these facts: guitar; beginner; rock; started in January. Answer
What do you do for fun?
and
How long have you been playing?
Your partner says,
I'm trying out a cooking class.
Ask one relevant follow-up. They answer,
It's fun, but a little expensive.
Respond without claiming you will join.
Use your own interest or an invented role. Explain the activity, one opinion, and when you started. Ask about the other person's interest.
Sample possibilities:
“I play guitar. I'm still learning. Mostly rock. I started in January.” / “What's the class like?” — “It's fun, but a little expensive.” — “Oh, okay. I've never tried a cooking class.”

Later, return without reading the model. Change the activity and the duration. Check whether you gave enough information for a follow-up and distinguished a tentative invitation from a confirmed plan.

note: For は期間、since は始めた時点を示します。上手でなくても、今取り組んでいることや感想を話せます。
